newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Price correction seen but downside limited.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Price correction seen but downside limited.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures are likely to face a technical correction following sharp rallies last week and the yen's moderate rebound after a weekend G7 meeting, traders said on Monday.
But they said that any fall will be limited by improving market sentiment and signs that Japan's rubber inventories are declining.
The G7 nations, meeting on the weekend in Berlin, said they favoured an end to the dollar's sharp rise.
One analyst at a commodity broker said nearby futures contracts will be supported by expectations of light deliveries at the spot expiry later this month.
The benchmark July contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended Monday's morning session at 156.9 yen per kg, against 157.3 yen per kg last Friday.
Similarly, the benchmark July contract on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 156.7 yen per kg in the second morning session, down from 157.4 yen last Friday.

"The sharp price rises last week were led by short-covering and the yen's steep depreciation, with few fresh factors detected. So it is natural for the markets to face a moderate correction," one trading house trader said.
"But falling rubber stocks, along with views that prices in producing countries are set to rebound, will likely prompt buying on any price falls," he said.

Japan's rubber inventories, which had cast a shadow on the market, have declined after hitting nearly three and six months high of 47,873 tonnes in end September in 1996, and the downward trends to sustain in the near-term, they said.

Japan's crude rubber stocks at the end of January this year amounted to 35,607 tonnes, down from 37,366 tonnes, but up from 29,680 tonnes in January 1996, according to the Japan Rubber Trade Association.

"I think Japan's rubber stocks are likely to fall to around 27,000 or 28,000 tonnes within next two months, backed by robust demand for news cars ahead of the tax hike," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
There was no offer prices from Thailand to Japan on Monday due to the the market holiday in Thailand due to Chinese Lunar New Year.

In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted higher at 165 yen per kg on Monday, in line with rises in rubber futures prices in Japan, compared with 157 yen on February 3.
